evidence.evidence_class: externally observed GitHub, public-network, and clean-clone state
observations: At the accepted commit these check runs completed with conclusion `success`: Quality, contracts, and packaging; Python 3.11; Python 3.12; Python 3.13; Compose configuration; Analyze python; Analyze javascript-typescript; Validate and package site; Deploy site.
A superseded `Deploy site` and `Validate and package site` pair shows `cancelled` at the same commit; they were replaced by the successful runs through the Pages concurrency group.

The CI wheel-isolation step now runs the installed distribution from a directory outside the checkout with a decoy `benchmarks/` beside the caller, so its success is evidence about the installed package rather than about the source tree. Before ESIO-DEF-001 was fixed this step ran from the repository root and could not have detected the defect.
Secret scanning, secret-scanning push protection, Dependabot security updates, private vulnerability reporting, and required web commit signoff were observed enabled.
`Dependency review` and `Commit signoff` run only on pull requests, were observed `success` there, and do not appear at this commit.

The branch ruleset grants the repository-admin role an `always` bypass so the bounded controller can push reconciled ledgers, so the required checks gate contributors and pull requests rather than the maintainer's own pushes.
Establishes that the declared checks passed in GitHub's hosted environment at this commit. It does not establish source truth, independent validation, or production readiness.

evidence.evidence_class: externally observed GitHub, public-network, and clean-clone state
observations: GitHub Pages is configured with `build_type: workflow`. The `Pages` workflow completed `success` and the newest `github-pages` deployment is bound to the accepted commit.
All nine deployed assets were fetched unauthenticated and their SHA-256 digests match, byte for byte, a site built from an independent clean clone of the published remote at this commit.

Those exact deployed bytes were driven in Chromium. Seven published scenarios behaved as documented: valid -> PERMIT_SCOPED_NEGATIVE / ABSENT_WITHIN_SCOPE; incomplete -> REJECT_NEGATIVE / PARTIAL; stale -> REJECT_NEGATIVE / ABSENT_WITHIN_SCOPE; ambiguous -> REJECT_NEGATIVE / NOT_OBSERVED; conflicting -> REJECT_NEGATIVE / CONTRADICTORY; tampered -> REJECT_UNVERIFIED_INPUT; invalid -> REJECT_INVALID_INPUT.
The demonstration keeps input rejection distinct from a gate rejection, so a malformed or tampered request is never presented as an evidential rejection of the negative claim.
No console error, page error, or failed request was recorded, and no internal anchor was broken.
The run control is reachable by keyboard alone and activates with Enter.
At a 375px viewport the document scroll width equals the client width.
Establishes deployed-artifact behaviour in one browser engine at two viewports. It is not a cross-browser test, an accessibility audit, or assistive-technology testing.

observations: 27 labels; milestone #1 `v0.6.0 - MVP research candidate`; six bounded MVP issues (#2-#7) linked to that milestone and to acceptance identifiers, of which #2 and #3 are closed with their evidence recorded in comments.

Branch ruleset `Default branch protection`: deletion, non-fast-forward, and required linear history blocked, nine required status checks, with an `always` bypass for the repository-admin role so the bounded controller can push reconciled ledgers. Tag ruleset `Release tag immutability`: deletion, update, and non-fast-forward blocked on `refs/tags/v*` with no bypass actor. This was demonstrated in practice: `v0.6.0` was published and then found to carry ESIO-DEF-001, and it could not be moved or removed.

Public GitHub Project `Evidence-State I/O roadmap` at https://github.com/users/redxking/projects/9, reachable unauthenticated, listed under Repository projects on this repository's Projects tab, carrying issues #2-#7. Its README states that item state is work state, not validated evidence. It was created through the web interface because the maintainer's CLI token lacks the `project` scope.

Establishes that the governance, security, community, and project-management surfaces exist and are populated. It does not establish that any item is validated, that the rules were exercised against an adversary, or that a closed issue is evidence.

evidence.evidence_class: externally observed GitHub release state and released-artifact behaviour
observations: Release `v0.6.1 - MVP research candidate` is published, not a draft, not a prerelease, `isImmutable` is true, and it is the latest release.
The annotated tag object `3200aa3f51161c40f258e7ae880eed04456cbb07` points at commit `d6eebbe2fc6840b54a41d5ab2f6f587b9310fa41`, which is an ancestor of the default branch.

Six assets are attached: the wheel, the source distribution, SHA256SUMS, EVIDENCE-MANIFEST.json, SBOM.spdx.json, and LIMITATIONS.md. Both distributions were downloaded unauthenticated and `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS` reported OK for each.

EVIDENCE-MANIFEST.json binds tag `v0.6.1`, commit `d6eebbe2fc6840b54a41d5ab2f6f587b9310fa41`, source tree `5ae4d2d5c8b67954ccb1fd3dc23e945e3fbb2508`, version `0.6.1`, a clean tracked worktree, no runtime dependencies, and the two artifact digests and sizes. The recorded tree equals `git rev-parse <commit>^{tree}`.
The SPDX SBOM declares Apache-2.0, the exact purl, and a download location pinned to the released commit. The attached LIMITATIONS.md is byte-identical to `release/LIMITATIONS.md`.

Build provenance verifies: `gh attestation verify` returns a SLSA provenance v1 statement whose subjects are both released artifacts with matching SHA-256 digests, whose source repository is this repository, and whose signer is `.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v0.6.1`.

The released wheel carries the EmptyBench corpus and oracle (2 matching entries in the wheel and 2 in the source distribution, against 0 in v0.6.0). Installed into a fresh Python 3.11 environment and run from a directory outside any checkout that also contains a decoy `benchmarks/` directory, `evidence-state --help` and `evidence-state demo --all --pretty` both succeed, reporting 24/24 cases passed, 12/12 matched pairs discriminated, zero unsafe permits, and zero false rejections, byte-identical to the same command run from the repository root. This is the direct check that ESIO-DEF-001 is fixed in the published artifact rather than only in the source tree.

The release workflow's own gate required every acceptance row other than MVP-ACC-025 to be PASS at the tagged commit, and verified stable SemVer, tag-to-package-version equality, and default-branch ancestry.

`v0.6.0` remains published and immutable and still carries ESIO-DEF-001. Its release notes now open with a warning that names the defect, states that its artifacts should not be used, and links this release. The tag ruleset blocks deletion, update, and non-fast-forward on `refs/tags/v*` with no bypass actor, which is why the defective release could not be withdrawn.

Establishes the release binding and that the published artifact behaves correctly wherever it is run. It does not establish source truth, independent custody, benchmark freezing, external reproduction, or production readiness.
